spots.name: St. Mary's Church, Lübeck
spots.summary: The Lübeck Marienkirche is a medieval basilica in the city centre of Lübeck, Germany. Built between 1265 and 1352, the church is located on the highest point of Lübeck's old town island within the Hanseatic merchants' quarter, which extends uphill from the warehouses on the River Trave to the church.

spots.name: Holsten Gate
spots.summary: The Holsten Gate is a city gate marking off the western boundary of the old center of the Hanseatic city of Lübeck. Built in 1464, the Brick Gothic construction is one of the relics of Lübeck's medieval city fortifications and one of two remaining city gates, the other being the Citadel Gate (Burgtor).

spots.name: Lübeck Cathedral
spots.summary: Lübeck Cathedral is a large brick-built Lutheran cathedral in Lübeck, Germany, and part of the Lübeck World Heritage Site. It was started in 1173 by Henry the Lion as a cathedral for the Bishop of Lübeck.

spots.name: Bad Schwartau
spots.summary: Bad Schwartau is the largest city in the district of Ostholstein, in Schleswig-Holstein, Germany. It is situated on the river Trave and the Schwartau creek, approximately 5 kilometres (3.1 mi) north of the Hanseatic City of Lübeck. Bad Schwartau is a spa-city, well known for its iodide saline waters.

spots.name: St Peter's Church, Lübeck
spots.summary: St. Peter's Church is a place of worship in Lübeck, Germany, that was first mentioned in 1170. Over the centuries, it was rebuilt several times until construction of the church was completed in the 15th century. During the Second World War, St.

spots.name: St. Jakobi
spots.summary: St. James' Church is one of the five main Evangelical Lutheran parish churches in Lübeck's old town, Germany.

spots.name: Hospital of the Holy Spirit
spots.summary: The Hospital of the Holy Spirit is a former hospital in Lübeck, Schleswig-Holstein, Germany.

spots.name: Salzspeicher
spots.summary: The Salzspeicher, of Lübeck, Germany, are six historic brick buildings on the Upper Trave River next to the Holstentor.

spots.name: Lübeck city hall
spots.summary: Its architecture is a stylistic potpourri reaching back to the 12th century. It is still the seat of the city administration and not a museum, so you can't have a look inside on your own. But there are guided tours every hour or so where the many historic rooms and the gallery of city leaders' portraits are explained (in German and possibly other languages).

spots.summary: Dedicated to the brothers Thomas and Heinrich Mann, who spent their youth there. It contains many of their works. Closed until 2023.

spots.name: Burgtor
spots.summary: The Burgtor, built 1444 in late Gothic style, was the northern city gate of Hanseatic Lübeck, now in Germany. It is one of two towered gates remaining from the medieval fortifications, the other being the more famous Holstentor.

spots.name: European Hansemuseum
spots.summary: The European Hansemuseum is a museum in Lübeck, Germany dedicated to the history of the Hanseatic League. Covering an area of in total 7,405 square metres (79,710 sq ft), is the largest museum in the world specifically dedicated to this subject. The museum was opened in May 2015.

spots.name: Aegidienkirche, Lübeck
spots.summary: The St.-Aegidien-Kirche or Aegidienkirche is a church building in the north German city of Lübeck, dedicated to saint Giles. It is the smallest and easternmost church in the city centre.

spots.name: Günter Grass House
spots.summary: Dedicated to the author (born in Gdańsk) who spent most of his life in Lübeck until his death in 2015 and who received the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1999.

spots.name: Burgtor Cemetery
spots.summary: Burgtor Cemetery or Burgtorfriedhof, originally the Allgemeine Gottesacker, is the successor to other cemeteries in Burgtor, Lübeck suburb of St. Gertrud. It was officially opened in 1834 and today covers an area of around eight hectares and around 8700 burial sites.

spots.name: Willy Brandt House
spots.summary: The Willy-Brandt-Haus in Lübeck is a museum and a memorial to the late politician Federal Chancellor and Nobel Peace Prize Laureate, Willy Brandt, of the Social Democratic Party of Germany (SPD).

spots.name: Behnhaus
spots.summary: The Behnhaus is an art museum in the Hanseatic city of Lübeck, Germany, and part of its World Heritage Site.

spots.name: Lübeck Academy of Music
spots.summary: The Lübeck Academy of Music in Lübeck, Germany, is the only higher level music school in the northernmost state of Schleswig-Holstein. The school is located in the World Heritage city of Lübeck, a historic hanseatic city. The school was founded in 1973 but its tradition goes back to 1911.

spots.name: Lübeck Museum of Theatre Puppets
spots.summary: The Lübeck Museum of Theatre Puppets is a museum of international puppetry in the Hanseatic city of Lübeck, Germany.

spots.name: Bucu
spots.summary: Bucu or Buku is a hill island surrounded by the Trave and Wakenitz Rivers in Lübeck, Germany. It is also the name of a medieval Slavic castle, now ruined, on the island. Count Adolf II of Holstein founded Lübeck on the island in 1143. The Burgkloster, or fortified monastery, of Lübeck is located atop the ruins of Bucu.

spots.summary: The Sacred Heart Church is the main Roman Catholic church in Lübeck. It was built in 1888 and consecrated on 10 May 1891.

spots.name: Theater Lübeck
spots.summary: The Theater Lübeck is one of the largest theaters in the German state of Schleswig-Holstein. It is managed by Theater Lübeck GmbH, a state-owned company of the Hansestadt Lübeck.

spots.name: Museumshafen Lubeck
spots.summary: It features some old-fashioned ships, among them a rebuilt Hanseatic kraweel ("Lisa von Lübeck") — more so in winter, because many of these ships are still in use during summer.

spots.name: Museum für Natur und Umwelt Lübeck
spots.summary: A natural history museum featuring, among other things, an entire sperm whale skeleton taken from an unlucky whale that died in a beaching incident.

spots.name: Oberschule zum Dom
spots.summary: The Oberschule zum Dom, a grammar school in Lübeck and the Schleswig-Holstein area of Germany was founded in 1905 during the final years of the German Empire under Kaiser Wilhelm II. The school survived the bombing carried out on the city of Lübeck by the Royal Air Force during the second world war.
